findings.claim: Loop 6 regression, and a new instance of earlier concern 2 (the drawn size changed by scale, rotate, translate or zoom). The new identity() helper (lines 146-151) accepts scale 1, rotate 0, translate 0, an identity matrix and zoom 1 as unscaled. That is right for a finished animation that holds its end value. It is also applied to endless animations, which are measured as drawn at one instant (lines 140-144). An ordinary short endless pulse whose keyframes start and end at the identity value now reads as unscaled whenever the sampled instant is at or near its start. I added one rule at a time to a fresh private copy of the completed work. Each rule was a 1 to 3 second endless pulse with its identity value at 0% and a smaller scale in between. (a) Individual scale on both tags: task 11 passed 4 of 8 runs at 89161df6 and 0 of 7 with the ea630d09 test file. (b) A transform pulse on both tags: 5 of 7 runs at 89161df6, 0 of 7 at ea630d09. (c) An individual-scale pulse on .site-aside: 7 of 7 at 89161df6 (all 12 tests passed), 0 of 7 at ea630d09. I loaded each page with no test handling in the pinned Chromium and read it four times between 0.3s and about 5s. Both tags were drawn at a width other than 200px at every reading, and the unmodified completed work was drawn at 200px at every reading. The checklist case is deterministic because of how the test is built. The pinned inline styles on .site-aside, including scale: none !important (the pinned() helper from line 153 and the loop that applies it to the checklist), are never restored: lines 213-218 restore only transition. In the second window both the checklist identity check and the tags' drawn-width check therefore see a forced unscaled checklist, so the only live check is the first sample, near the pulse's identity start. So a page that README task 11 forbids can pass, and for the tag cases the same page passes or fails from run to run, which is flaky feedback. Graded medium, not high, on the cl4-sme-001 / cl5-edu-001 precedent: it needs an animation the README now forbids, and the calculated width is still required, because the base style is what is measured. It differs from the owner-accepted residual (cl5-edu-001, cl5-sme-001) in three ways. It is a regression introduced by loop 6. It is nondeterministic. The edit is more plausible, because a short decorative pulse is not a paused, long-delayed, very long or slow animation or an animated custom property. Neither the lab.json examples (paused, delayed, very long) nor the solved-run record's 'not covered' list names it. The record's matrix lists 'an endless scale animation' as a failing variant, but it has no endless variant that starts at its identity value.
findings.recommendation: Accept identity end values only for animations the test has just finished, and for static declarations. For an element that still has a running animation after finite ones are finished (an endless one), keep the ea630d09 rule: any transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom other than none or 1 fails. Restore .site-aside's pinned inline styles after each window, as is already done for transition, so that the second window's checklist checks are live. Add endless pulses that start at their identity value, on the tags and on the checklist, to the solved-run matrix. Run each one several times.

findings.claim: After loop 6, three descriptions of the task 11 test no longer match its behaviour or the README rule. (1) The lab.json notes still say the test 'rejects the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties'. Static identity values on the tags and the checklist now pass all 12 tests (probe: an identity matrix, rotate 0deg, translate 0px, scale 1 and zoom 100% on the tags, plus translateX(0), scale 1 1 and rotate z 0deg on the checklist). It now rejects only values other than identity. (2) The notes' 'finite animations finished first' is still not scoped to the checklist and the two tags. A finite scale entrance on .page is still measured mid-flight and fails task 11 with 'something around it is scaling it'. (3) The solved-run record lists 'short filled entrance animations on the tags and on the checklist' and 'learner transitions on the checklist and tag sizes' as valid variants. README task 11 Outcome now says that no animation or transition may change the size, position or scale of the checklist or the tags, so the README forbids what the record calls valid. Also, one form of checklist entrance, a combined transform and zoom entrance, fails task 5 with the unrelated message 'Below 1000px wide, the gear checklist is not stacked after the trails' (4 of 4 runs), while transform-only, zoom-only and individual-property entrances pass. Graded low. The learner-facing README is the stricter text, so these mismatches never let a learner who follows it fail or pass wrongly; they mislead only readers of lab.json and the evidence record.
findings.recommendation: In the lab.json notes say that the test rejects transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom values other than identity, and that finite animations are finished on the checklist and the two tags only. In the next solved-run record, call the filled entrance and transition variants 'accepted by the test though README task 11 asks for a static layout', not 'valid'.

items.note: Judged on the text, as the owner accepted the residual. README line 17 now adds 'It does not catch every animation, so task 11 also asks you to keep the checklist layout static.' Task 11 Outcome (line 141) states that rule and its scope: no animation or transition may change the size, position or scale of the checklist, the two tags or any element around them that affects their layout, and decorative effects elsewhere are fine. The lab.json notes (line 87) say that the test does not detect every animation that changes the drawn size later, give paused, delayed and very long ones as examples, and say that the README asks for a static layout. A learner who follows the README cannot be misled into thinking a held animation is acceptable, and the stated scope is fair to decorative work elsewhere on the page. The new short endless pulse route is a separate loop-6 regression, filed as cl6-edu-001, and is not counted against this item.
